card.source: Cairns, Hass-Klau & Goodwin, 'Traffic Impact of Highway Capacity Reductions: Assessment of the Evidence' (Landor, 1998)
card.claim: When road capacity is removed, part of the traffic does not reappear elsewhere ('traffic evaporation'), but the share varies widely from case to case.

card.source: Evaluations of the 2016 closure of the Voie Georges-Pompidou (Paris right-bank lower quays)
card.claim: After the lower quays closed, monitoring reported traffic shifting onto nearby parallel routes, including the upper quays, alongside a debate about how much traffic evaporated.

card.source: Evaluations of London Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (e.g. Goodman et al., 2021)
card.claim: The effect of filtering streets on surrounding roads differs from site to site, so displacement onto other streets has to be checked locally rather than assumed away.
Residential streets have a limited 'environmental capacity': beyond a certain traffic level, living conditions degrade even if the street can physically carry more vehicles.

brief.target: Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville from Rue de Brosse to Pont Louis-Philippe

hypothesis.text: Closing the eastbound Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville will cut traffic on that segment by ≥70% under normal demand.
Displaced eastbound traffic will spill onto the top-ranked detour Rue François Miron (a living_street/residential) exceeding both the 30% and 100 veh/h thresholds.
The second-ranked detour Rue de Brosse (living_street) will also see a residential spillover breach (>30% and >100 veh/h).
Network-wide delay will rise by >10% and >20 veh·h as traffic redistributes onto narrower parallel streets.
A modal filter on Rue François Miron (F1) will eliminate its C1 breach without triggering new C1/C2/C3 violations elsewhere at DN demand.
Adding a second modal filter on Rue de Brosse (F12) will resolve the remaining residential spillover without creating fresh failures at DN demand.

decision.rationale: First run the baseline closure under normal demand to measure target‑segment reduction (G1) and check for robust C1 spillover on Rue François Miron and Rue de Brosse, which determines whether to proceed to mitigation or robustness.

decision.rationale: Baseline quays:FC.M0.DN achieves G1 but exhibits robust C1 violations on Rue François Miron (213 vs base 43.7) and Rue de Brosse (186.3 vs base 15.7), exceeding the 30% and 100 veh/h thresholds in all three seeds, confirming spillover that requires mitigation.

Test modal filter on Rue François Miron (F1) at normal demand to see if it eliminates the observed C1 spillover (>30% & >100 veh/h) while preserving the ≥70% reduction on the closed quay and avoiding new major/critical violations.

decision.rationale: F1 introduced critical gridlock (C3) and major delay (C2); testing a single modal filter on the second‑ranked detour Rue de Brosse (F2) may resolve its spillover without triggering new violations.

decision.rationale: F1 and F2 each removed their targeted C1 spillover but introduced critical gridlock (C3) and major delay (C2) violations at DN demand; testing the combined modal filter F12 will reveal whether it can resolve both residential spillovers without adding new major/critical violations.

events.label: Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville from Rue de Brosse to Pont Louis-Philippe closed to eastbound cars, modal filters on Rue François Miron and Rue de Brosse, normal demand
Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville from Rue de Brosse to Pont Louis-Philippe closed to eastbound cars, modal filters on Rue François Miron and Rue de Brosse, normal demand

decision.rationale: No mitigation (F1, F2, F12) succeeded at normal demand due to new C2/C3 violations; we now test the bare policy across demands to assess robustness—starting with low demand to see if spillover reduces before checking high demand.

Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville from Rue de Brosse to Pont Louis-Philippe closed to eastbound cars, low demand

decision.rationale: All tested mitigations (F1, F2, F12) at normal demand eliminate the targeted C1 spillover but introduce critical gridlock (C3) and major delay (C2) violations, so none are worth pursuing; we proceed to robustness testing of the bare policy across demand levels.

Baseline policy shows robust C1 spillover at normal demand; all modal-filter mitigations eliminate spillover but introduce critical/major violations (gridlock/delay). To assess robustness before reporting, we must test the bare policy at high demand (DH) to see if violations persist or worsen.
